title: Building Better Conservation Infrastructure in the Appalachian Coalfields
description: Engage 60 partners in cross-boundary collaborations and strategic planning to create a Coordinated Interagency Conservation Partnership (CICP) to address challenges preventing the implementation of conservation actions benefiting at-risk species, habitats and communities. Project will engage stakeholders to form the framework of the CICP followed by implementing small pilot strategies to refine the framework, restore and connect habitats, and sustain communities through future projects.

title: Increasing the Scale of Red Spruce Ecosystem Restoration in Central Appalacian Highlands
description: Restore more than 5,000 acres of red spruce forest and 45 miles of headwater streams in the Central Appalachian Highlands through release treatments, planting and stream restoration. Project will build restoration workforce capacity, develop best practices, monitor outcomes and conduct outreach to expand red spruce ecosystem restoration across the region.

title: Developing Giant Rivercane Restoration for the Southeastern United States
description: Develop giant rivercane seed stock with accompanying genetic information and public database to assist Tribal Nations and other stakeholders in implementing rivercane habitat restoration projects across the Southeast. Project will increase Tribal Nation capacity to manage and access a resource that is a cultural keystone species and part of many Southeastern Indigenous communities' culture, heritage and lifeways.

title: $7.5 Million for Airport Improvements
description:
North Central West Virginia Airport, Clarksburg - Construct Terminal Access Road $1,064,089

Elkins/Randolph County (Jennings Randolph Field), Elkins - Obstruction Marking\Lighting\Removal $116,500

Morgantown Municipal/Walter L Bill Hart Field, Morgantown - Extend/Expand Runway $6,302,717

title: Four WV School Systems Selected for Clean School Bus Program Awards
description: Four school systems in West Virginia (Calhoun, McDowell, Randolph, and Summers Counties) were selected by the EPA’s Clean School Bus (CSB) Program to receive rebates for the replacement of existing school buses with zero-emission and clean buses. These systems will receive a total of $1.8 million to replace five school buses with cleaner alternatives that will help to improve air quality inside the buses, within bus loading areas, and throughout the communities in which they operate. These bus replacements will also result in reduced health risks and reduced fuel and maintenance costs within the selected counties.

title: $62,000 Awarded Through Litter Control Grant Program
description: Fourteen applicants were selected for awards totaling $62,000 for the FY2025 cycle of the Litter Control Grant program. This program is a matching fund administered by the WV Department of Environmental Protection, with funding provided by litter fines, that assists municipalities and county government agencies with community cleanup and litter enforcement projects. These awards will go towards funding cleanup costs, enforcement, and preventive measures to assist with litter control across the Mountain State.

title: WV Projects Awarded Over $36 Million Through RAISE Grant Program
description: On June 26, 2024, the Department of Transportation (DOT) announced that $1.8 billion had been awarded to 148 of the projects submitted to the Rebuilding American Infrastructure with Sustainability and Equity (RAISE) discretionary grant program this year, including three projects in West Virginia which were awarded a total of $36,750,000. RAISE is a DOT program established by the IIJA to invest in road, rail, transit and port projects that promise to achieve national objectives. The awards received by the Mountain State will fund improvements to roadway infrastructure and new bicycle and pedestrian facilities on critical corridors in the cities of Charleston and Beckley and planning for future corridor upgrades in the city of Westover. These projects will help to promote the safety of all transportation users and improve connectivity within these communities.

title: $87.5 Million Awarded for Bridge Replacement on West Virginia-Ohio Border
description: The West Virginia Division of Highways (WVDOH) has been awarded $87.5 million through the Bridge Investment Program to fully replace the deteriorating Market Street Bridge and reopen a major thoroughfare that connects Ohio and West Virginia. Built in 1905, this almost 120-year-old structure was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2019, and has sat in limbo for nearly seven months after its closure in December 2023 due to continuing structural issues. The bridge links West Virginia Route 2 with Ohio Route 7 and acts as a traffic reliever for its northern neighbor, the Veterans Memorial Bridge, which carries U.S. Route 22 across the Ohio River. This is a major win for both the WVDOH and the Ohio Department of Transportation, which worked together to secure funding for the replacement. The project is expected to be completed within the next 10 years and will provide a critical connection between communities in West Virginia and Ohio.

title: ARC Awards $33.5 Million to Accelerate Economic Growth Across 13 Appalachian States
description: The Appalachian Regional Commission awarded a total of $33.5 million to 12 collaborative, multi-state projects that will bring together more than 145 partners across all 13 Appalachian states to strengthen workforce and educational opportunities, infrastructure and entrepreneurship. Out of these 12 projects, seven will directly impact West Virginia communities.

title: Wheeling Receives $5 Million Award for a New Visitors Center
agency: Department of Housing and Urban Development
description: The Wheeling Convention and Visitors Bureau has been awarded a $5 million dollar Community Project Funding Award administered by the Department of Housing and Urban Development for the Wheeling Gateway Visitors Center. The project will transform the site of the former Wheeling Inn into a new Visitors and Heritage Center, honoring the history of Wheeling.

title: EDA Invests $6.6 Million in West Virginia Communities Through the Assistance to Coal Communities Program
description:
The McDowell County Public Service District and the Benedum Airport Authority were awarded a total of $6.6 million through the Economic Development Administration's Assistance to Coal Communities program.

A $3.4 million investment for the McDowell County Public Service District will support water infrastructure improvements, including new waterlines in areas throughout McDowell County. The Benedum Airport Authority will receive $3.2 million to support the construction of four parking lots with sidewalk access and overhead lighting in Bridgeport, West Virginia. Once completed, these projects will help create new job opportunities in their regions to boost economic development, diversify the local economies, and advance economic resiliency.

The Assistance to Coal Communities program supports communities and regions that have been negatively impacted by changes in the coal economy. These funds are awarded on a competitive basis to projects and activities that support economic diversification, job creation, capital investment, workforce development, and re-employment opportunities. The EDA prioritizes applications that will produce multiple economic and workforce development outcomes and that are specifically identified under local and regional economic development plans.

title: $5.3 Million Awarded by Department of Commerce to Support Local Economic Development Efforts
description:
The U.S. Department of Commerce's Economic Development Administration (EDA) recently invested a total of $5.3 million in four organizations in West Virginia to support infrastructure improvements, workforce development, and technical assistance strategies.

The grantees of this investment are Greenbrier County Airport Authority in Lewisburg, the Marshall University Research Corporation in Huntington, Eastern West Virginia Community and Technical College in Moorefield, and West Virginia University Research Corporation in Morgantown. This investment from EDA will create about 240 jobs and generate nearly $60 million in private investments, helping to bolster the economy of the Mountain State.

title: $25 Million SS4A Award for Transportation Improvements in Bluefield
description:
The city of Bluefield, West Virginia was awarded over $25 million through the Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) program for the “Making Residents, Students, and Visitors Safer in the Education and Recreation District” project. This project will enhance safety and greatly improve accommodations for residents, students, and visitors walking, biking, and rolling in the project area, which encompasses African American communities and is the main entrance to Bluefield State University along U.S. Route 52.

The City received a 2022 SS4A grant to develop a Comprehensive Safety Action Plan, which it completed and adopted in February 2024, and views this project location as the potential backbone upon which other Action Plan-identified projects can be built.

title: WV Organizations Receive $19 Million in Awards from Appalachian Regional Commission
description:
The Appalachian Regional Commission awarded a total of $19 million to 14 projects across the state through the Partnerships for Opportunity and Workforce and Economic Revitalization (POWER) program.

One of these projects, developed by the West Virginia Department of Economic Development in partnership with the WV Workforce Resiliency Office and private childcare development firm Wonderschool, will launch two new programs to increase accessible and affordable childcare supply, empower childcare providers to attract and retain childcare workers, and improve career pathways for childcare workers in eight counties.

title: U.S. Department of Energy Awards $9.8 million for Iron Phosphate Manufacturing in Bridgeport, WV
description:
Sparkz Inc. received a $9.8 million award from the U.S. Department of Energy to redevelop a closed manufacturing facility in Bridgeport, WV into a first-of-its-kind battery-grade iron phosphate (FePO4) plant. This is one of 14 projects selected from coal communities across the nation to receive funding to address energy supply chain vulnerabilities and accelerate domestic clean energy manufacturing.

Iron Phosphate is a precursor material for the manufacture of Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles and is not currently manufactured in the U.S. In addition to establishing a domestic supply chain for LFP production, this award will directly benefit the community of Bridgeport and the greater Taylor County area by creating 75 high quality jobs. Sparkz is working with the United Mine Workers of America Labor Union and the West Virginia Economic Development Authority to recruit, hire, and train members of the local community.

title: WVDOH Awarded $985,000 Accelerated Innovation Deployment (AID) Demonstration Grant
description: The West Virginia Division of Highways (WVDOH) was awarded over $985,000 through FHWA's Accelerated Innovation Deployment Demonstration program. This award will be used to replace the Purgitsville Bridge, a heavily used bridge in a rural portion of Hampshire County that has significant deficiencies requiring bridge deck replacement. The WVDOH will use Orthotropic Steel Deck technology for this replacement, which offers an efficient and cost-effective solution that extends the bridge service life and improves safety and traffic mobility during construction.

title: USDA Awards West Virginia Department of Human Services Grant to Strengthen the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program
description:
The Department of Human Services (DoHS), in coordination with the Bureau of Family Assistance and the Office of the Inspector General, was awarded a $331,424 SNAP Fraud Framework Implementation grant. This program supports efforts to improve and expand recipient fraud prevention, detection, and investigation efforts.

West Virginia is one of only 10 states awarded a SNAP Fraud Framework Implementation Grant this year. With this funding, the DoHS will implement a Case Management and Fraud Reduction system to track investigative caseloads and develop a SNAP Recipient Integrity Education program that will explain SNAP fraud and associated penalties to prevent households from committing or becoming victims of program violations.

title: Office of Broadband Receives $9 Million State Digital Equity Capacity Grant
description:
West Virginia was approved to receive over $9 million through the National Telecommunications and Information Administration's State Digital Equity Capacity Program. This program provides funding to states to implement their Digital Equity Plans, which identify barriers to digital equity and outline strategies for states to provide the tools and skills necessary to benefit from access to high-speed Internet service.

With this funding, the West Virginia Office of Broadband will implement a variety of initiatives to improve digital equity in the state. These include launching a Digital Skills program to provide training, education, and online resources to West Virginians; an affordable device program for eligible residents; and funding for local governments to create their own specialized digital equity plans.

title: Winchester & Western Railroad Awarded $22.8 million from Federal Railroad Administration
description: The Winchester & Western Railroad was awarded almost $22.8 million through the Federal Railroad Administration's Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program. This award will fund the rehabilitation of segments of the Winchester & Western Railroad mainline in West Virginia and Maryland to eliminate all remaining legacy rail and old tie structure. This project will enhance the safety, efficiency, and resiliency of this line as it is returned to a state of good repair.

title: Three WV Communities Receive Awards through Safe Streets and Roads for All Program
description: The U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) has awarded $992,000 through the Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) program to enhance road safety in three West Virginia Communities. This funding will be used to develop safety action plans focused on reducing fatal and injury crashes and improving overall safety on roadways in Martinsburg, Star City, and Wheeling.

title: Low Carbon Transportation Materials - $30.5M
description: The West Virginia Department of Transportation was awarded over $30.5 million from the U.S. Department of Transportation's Low Carbon Transportation Materials program to modernize transportation systems across the state. Under this program, state Departments of Transportation can establish new processes to implement and use American-made, low carbon materials on Federal-aid transportation projects. Awarded agencies are provided with reimbursement and incentive funding to purchase these construction materials, including asphalt, glass, steel, and concrete. These activities will bolster economic development in communities across the country and encourage manufacturers to reduce industrial emissions.

title: $179,968 to Improve the Data Interpretation Process in Forensic Fire Debris Analysis
